Development of Superhydrophobic Coatings on Jute Using Graphene and Reduce Graphene oxide Based Nanocomposites

Abstract:

The development of sustainable multifunctional materials that combine electrical conductivity, water repellency, and mechanical flexibility is of significant interest for next-generation wearable and environmental technologies. In this study, a bioinspired superhydrophobic and electrically conductive jute fiber was fabricated through a sequential coating strategy involving a graphene/reduced graphene oxide (graphene/rGO) conductive network, a SiO2&ndashboric acid&ndashchitosan hierarchical roughness layer, and dual-silane surface modification using hexamethyldisilazane (HMDS) and hexadecyltrimethoxysilane (HDTMS). Natural jute was selected as the substrate owing to its biodegradability, low cost, and intrinsic fibrous microstructure. Graphene and rGO established an interconnected conductive pathway, while SiO2 nanoparticles generated hierarchical micro/nanostructures that enhanced surface roughness. Chitosan acted as a bio-based binder, whereas boric acid chemically reinforced the chitosan matrix, improving coating adhesion, durability, and thermal stability. The final HMDS/HDTMS treatment significantly reduced the surface free energy by introducing hydrophobic methyl and long alkyl functional groups. Structural and chemical characterization using FESEM, EDX, XRD, Raman spectroscopy, and FTIR confirmed the successful formation of the multilayer coating and uniform surface morphology. The fabricated jute fiber exhibited excellent superhydrophobicity with a static water contact angle of 158 &plusmn 6&deg, attributed to the synergistic effect of hierarchical roughness and low surface energy, consistent with the Cassie&ndashBaxter wetting mechanism. The coating also demonstrated uniform surface morphology, mechanical robustness, and stable conductive pathways, making it suitable for repeated use under flexible conditions. The combination of sustainable natural fibers with conductive carbon nanomaterials and environmentally benign surface modification provides a simple, scalable, and cost-effective strategy for fabricating multifunctional materials. The developed superhydrophobic conductive jute fiber shows considerable potential for applications in wearable electronics, flexible sensors, smart textiles, electromagnetic interference shielding, oil&ndashwater separation, and self-cleaning environmental systems.
